newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 24.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Australian blunders again test relations: Trans-Tasman relations took a further dive on Wednesday -- on the eve of Prime Minister Jim Bolger's visit to Melbourne -- with another leak of Australian Government papers patronising the New Zealand Government. Page 1.

Treasury: tax-cut link political tactic: The Treasury revealed on Wednesday that the linking of future tax cuts to the outcome of the retirement savings scheme referendum -- as agreed under the Coalition accord -- is a purely political tactic
without fiscal logic. Page 2.
Business leaders urge separating issues: Tax cuts would be good for the economy and should be considered separately from the compulsory retirement savings scheme, business leaders say. Page 2.

Committee meets to consider Kopu's future: Parliament's privileges committee is to meet this afternoon to consider independent Maori MP Alamein Kopu's right to remain as an MP, but Kopu will not be there. Page 2.
Kopu's use of Maori challenged: Labour list MP Dover Samuels has accused dissident MP Alamein Kopu of using the Maori language to score political points. Page 2.

Lawyers in real estate 'cheaper': Lawyers would be able to do the work of real estate agents for a much cheaper price if the law was changed to open up the job to competition, according to Law Society president Ian Haynes. Page 15.
PDL profit up 73 pct: Electrical and plastics manufacturer PDL Holdings boosted first-quarter profit by 73 percent and expects a strong second three months. Page 15.

No funds for tax cuts after 98, says banker: Planned tax cuts will be called off after 1998 because the government will barely break even in its 1988-99 financial year, according to merchant bankers Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. Page 15.

Tradenz monitors Asian currencies' effect on exports: Tradenz in Singapore is monitoring the weakening of currencies in Asian countries and how that will affect the $2 billion of New Zealand exports to the east Asian region. Page 15.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Henare blasts Australians as 'mongrels': The Minister of Maori Affairs, Tau Henare, on Wednesday described Australians as "a pack of mongrels" over Canberra's leaked briefing paper on Pacific neighbours and called for an apology from the Australian Government.

Britomart publicity queried: Britomart developer Pacific Capital Assets began promoting its $100 million float among New Zealand brokers at private functions on Wednesday, but the nature of the promotion raises questions on the application of the Securities Act.
US firm buys Armourguard: A United States multinational, Tyco Internation, has bought the country's largest security firm, Armourguard, from Freightways.

INL rethinks Sky aspirations: Independent Newspapers, in the throes of buying a 51 percent holding in Sky Network Television, is believed to be contemplating cutting its prospective holding to 40 percent.

Kiwi Income was eyeing Nat Mutual Centre: Kiwi Income Property Trust says in its annual report it was looking at a potential interest in the 19-storey National Mutual Centre on Shortland Street when it bought into the Lion Nathan proprty across the road early last year.
THE PRESS
Misery for homeowners: Homeowners are steeling themselves for a round of substantial interest rate rises after the first of the major leaders made its move on Wednesday. Page 1.
Fines up, fatals down as hidden speed cameras go to work: The trial of hidden speed cameras has had a spectacular and lucrative start for the Ministry of Transport. Page 1.
Treaty issues control Kopu's agenda: Alliance defector Alamein Kopu, on the eve of her privileges committee hearing has vowed that she will not remain silent on Treaty of Waitangi issues. Page 2.
Henare accuses MP of stealing: Maori Affairs Minister Tau Henare used the cover of Parliamentary privilege on Wednesday to accuse Labour MP Trevor Mallard of stealing Tuku Morgan's diary. Page 3.

Leaked paper targets Peters: New Zealand on Wednesday night played down the significance of leaked papers revealing Australian strategies to increase New Zealand defence spending, as the Australian Government reeled in the wake of its second diplomatic blunder in a week. Page 3.
Kiwi dollar's rodeo ride tests Reserve Bank: The kiwi dollar's wild ride on Wednesday pushed around 90-day interest rates and tested the Reserve Bank's nerve. Page 35.
Peters paints rosy forecast: New Zealand's Treasurer, Winston Peters, on Wednesday stood by Treasury's rosy economic forecasts. Page 35.

'Millennium bug' could be costly for directors: Company directors could face fines of up to $200,000 if they did not assess and try to fix 2000 computer problems in their organisations, a Wellington lawyer, Craig Jones, said on Wednesday. Page 35.
